questions.question: If you are backing up and are unsure about where you are going, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and get out to look.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and get out to look.
questions.explanation: If you are unsure about your path while backing, stop the vehicle and get out to check your path before continuing.

questions.question: What happens when you push in the trailer air supply control?

options.text: Air is sent to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air is sent to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: What is the Johnson bar?

options.text: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes
A valve that shows the fuel level
A valve that limits how much cargo you can carry

questions.correctAnswerText: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes
questions.explanation: The Johnson bar (also called the trolley valve or trailer hand valve) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving could cause a skid.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: To speed up in rural areas.
Only to test the trailer brakes.
At the same time as the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) should only be used to test the brakes. Using it while driving could cause a skid.

questions.question: How much space should there be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
questions.correctAnswerText: No space
questions.explanation: Before each trip, check all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: What happens when you push in the trailer air supply control?

options.text: Air is sent to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air is sent to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: What does an air supply control in the "emergency" position do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Applies the trailer emergency brakes.
questions.explanation: When an air supply control is set to the "emergency" position, the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes are applied.

questions.question: What does the tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Prevents the tractor from being stolen
Prevents the tractor from going too fast
Keeps air in the brakes if the trailer breaks away or leaks
Makes sure the engine is properly lubricated

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the brakes if the trailer breaks away or leaks
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak.

questions.question: How should you position the tractor when backing up to couple a trailer?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle in front of the trailer.
Directly in front of the trailer.
At a 30-degree angle in front of the trailer.
At a 60-degree angle in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: When backing up to couple a trailer, position the tractor directly in front of it. Backing at an angle could move the trailer and damage the landing gear.

questions.question: What is the tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if a bad leak happens
A valve that prevents the trailer from accidentally coming loose
A valve that keeps the vehicle from going too fast

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if a bad leak happens
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. The valve closes automatically if the pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: Bobtail tractors are ____ to stop than tractors with full semitrailers attached.
questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor has no semitrailer attached. When driving a bobtail, stopping is harder. It takes longer to come to a complete stop than when a tractor pulls a loaded semitrailer.

questions.question: Trailers with low underneath clearance can be difficult when driving over:
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are difficult to cross with a trailer that has low clearance. Low trailers and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers have the most trouble crossing raised railroad crossings.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle usually requires ____ than driving a single vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: More skill
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more driving skill than single vehicles. They are longer and heavier, making them more likely to roll over.

questions.question: Compared to other commercial vehicles, combination vehicles need more road space because they are longer and they:

options.text: Need more space to turn and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other commercial vehicles because they are longer and need more space to turn and stop. Managing space properly is important when driving a combination vehicle.

questions.question: To help prevent a rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Placed as high as possible inside a trailer.
Placed as low as possible inside a trailer.
Placed on the driver's side of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Placed as low as possible inside a trailer.
questions.explanation: Vehicles that are top-heavy are more likely to roll over. Keep cargo as low in the trailer as possible to reduce this risk.

questions.question: If the trailer begins to skid, the best action is to:

options.text: Quickly turn the steering wheel one way, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your trailer skids, release the brakes to help the wheels grip the road again. Once traction returns, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: When the wheels of a trailer lock up:
questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer may swing around.
questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, the trailer may swing out and hit other vehicles. This is most likely to happen with lightly-loaded trailers.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle ____ driving a single vehicle.

options.text: Is safer in bad weather than

questions.correctAnswerText: Requires more skill than
questions.explanation: Driving a combination vehicle requires more skill than driving a single vehicle. Combination vehicles are generally longer and heavier than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: Trailers built before 1975:

options.text: Are required to have spring brakes.
Are not required to have spring brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not required to have spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need to have spring brakes. When parking a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to keep it from rolling.

questions.question: Shut-off valves:

options.text: Prevent air from escaping the air brake system.
Prevent air from entering the air brake system.
Control vehicles that are out of control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent air from escaping the air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers in air supply lines. The rear shut-off valve should always be closed to keep air in the brake system.
